FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Connectors for Electronic Equipment and Telecommunication Division Council. by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics

This standard is one of the series of Indian Standards on low frequency connectors below 3 MHz used in electronic equipment and shall be read in conjunction with IS 9647 : I986 `General requirements and methods of test for low frcqucncy connectors below 3 MHz including dc (first revision )`. Subsequent parts of this standard will cover detail specification for specific types of connectors, assistance has been derived from IEC Pub 130-12 ( 1976 ) `Connectors While preparing this standard, for ~frequencies below 3MHz : Part 12 Link and test connectors', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. For the purpose of deciding whether a partrcular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expr~essing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

LINKANDTESTCONNECTORSSPECIFICATION
PART 1 SCOPE This standard specifies test schedule and requirements for following two series of link and test connectors: a) A series of the conventional wiring type, 1 TEST SCHEDULE AND REQUIREMENTS 4 MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP

The materials used and workmanship shall be in accordance with 4 of IS 9647 : 1986 in addition to the following materials: For two-way, three-way, sockets for conventional Insulators Contacts Plating : Moulded : Phosphor : 0.50 Micron four-way wiring: pbenolics bronze gold over Nickel and six-way

b) A series to be directly soldered on a printed board with a nominal thickness up to 1.6 mm ( 0.063 inches ) according to IS 7405 ( Part 1 ) : 1983, and c) U-Link plugs and cord plug.

NOTE - The terminations may be reduced of bent over after assembly to comply with IS X943 : 1978.

ANNEX C ( Table 3 )
MECHANICAL Test Mechanical endurance ( Short term ) test AND ELECTRICAL Specific ENDURANCE and TESTS ( SHORT TERM )

Test Condition Description

Requirements

Final measurements 1) Visual examination

A test product shall be fully inserted into the connector socket contacts and withdrawn for a total of 500 insertion and withdrawal cycles, at a rate not to exceed 100 cycles per hour. On completion, the following measurements shall be made: The specimens shall be visually examined. The specimen shall be connected as in Fig. C- 1. Measurement shall be made after the temperature of the wire has stabilised with the rated current flowing through the contacts. The potenshall be measured tial drop across each mated test product and connector between the two points indicated "X" - "X7' in Fig. C-l.

No mechanical deterioration such as would impair the operation. The voltage not greater volts. drop than shall be 20 mili-

Sockets shall be rigidly mounted in a manner to permit mating and unmating of the counter part connectors and with instrumentation capable of measuring the specified forces. Gradually inaxial load shall be creasing applied until plugs and sockets are in full engagement. Then the forces shall be applied so as to disengage the connectors. The forces shall be measured in both directions. 11

I$13984 ( Part 1 ) : 19P5 Specific Test Conditiort an ( Description A test product shall be fully inserted 3 times into the connector socket contact and withdrawn. The test product shall again be inserted and engagement and disengagement forces shall be measured. endurance Electrical ( Short term ) test The mated sets shall be exposed for a total period of 1000 h at the maximum temperature of the temperature severity. The temperature severity shall be T65/200 ( - 65�C cold ) and 200�C ( Dry heat ). During this period the contacts shall carry their rated current unless otherwise specified. For batch acceptance the duration of exposure shall be 168 hours. Final measurements Visual examination On completion of the test, followin& measurements shall be made: The specimens shall be visually examined. Test

No mechanical or electrical deterioration such as would impair the operation. ) This is same as for mechanical endurance test ( short term ) above. There shall be no break or flashover. down

Contact

resistance

Voltage

proof

The specimen shall be mounted as in Fig. C-2. The proof voltage shall be steadily increased `from zero to proof value at a rate of approximately 500 V ( rms or DC ) per set unless otherwise specified. Upon completion of the test, the proof voltage shall be gradually reduced to avoid voltage surges. The following details shall apply: Magnitude and nature of test voltage: At sea level 3 000 Vat ( rms ). 50 Hz ( for a period of 15 S). Points of application of test Between voltage: current carrying parts and ground. On multiple contact connectors, the voltage shall be applied between all contacts alternately connected.
